rationale: The pain is real — AI-generated message overload erodes team focus — but the buyer is vague ("knowledge workers at SMBs") and there is no credible willingness-to-pay signal: no one is currently spending money on filtering AI-generated Slack noise, and the natural home for this would be an HR-tech or productivity add-on with a long enterprise sales cycle. Operationally, any meaningful solution requires per-company customisation of what counts as "machine vs human" content, keeping autonomy low. Drop until the segment sharpens and a paid substitute emerges.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. The core concept — a Slack/Teams filter that tags or summarises AI-generated messages — is technically buildable as a Claude prompt + webhook + a simple config form, but the go-to-market is the blocking problem: there is no identifiable buyer with budget authority and no established category they already spend on. A solo non-technical operator would struggle to find, close, and onboard companies without significant sales effort. Revisit if a paid competitor emerges or the volume of complaints grows into a named category.
